assets.prompt: Use case: game-assets. Preview-only style revision for Korean game OnTop Skewer King. Edit image 1, the supplied existing artwork; image 2 is ONLY the actual game's geometry/palette/environment reference. The screenshot UI, countdown number, text and controls must NOT appear in the output. Restyle the ENTIRE scene into cohesive LOW-POLY 3D GAME ART: clearly visible broad polygon facets, simplified meshes, restrained bevels, matte flat-color materials, low-detail flat-shaded geometry, soft ambient occlusion, crisp silhouettes, warm gentle game lighting. This should look like a polished small Three.js VR mini-game or Blender low-poly render, not photorealism, not a photograph with a polygon filter, not a glossy Pixar movie. No photographic skin, detailed hair strands, cloth weave, grain textures, wet food shine, cheese drips, lens bokeh, heavy bloom, steam or sparks. Match game's honey-brown counter, dark green hanok curtain, cream polygon dishes. Food identities from real game: red low-poly cherry tomato, green angular bell-pepper cross-section, segmented curled pink shrimp, grilled brown beef morsel, thin yellow cheese wrap and salmon-pink bacon. Food must still look edible and recognizable, not plastic toy cubes or paper cutouts. Wide landscape 16:9 artwork, no UI frames, text, letters, logos or watermarks. Keep main subject within central 80% for future image-card cropping. IMAGE 1 EDIT TARGET: preserve the existing close-up composition of one bamboo skewer and two hands threading a green pepper piece. Convert both hands into stylized low-poly game-avatar hands with simple faceted fingers, no skin pores. Skewer holds one each tomato, shrimp, beef and a thin cheese sheet wrapping food. Main action clearly 'thread ingredients to match a pictured order'. Background order picture remains purely pictorial, no writing. Cream polygon dishes contain the same game's foods; simplified hanok wooden shelf and dark green curtain. Smaller thumbnail must immediately communicate food-skewer assembly. Keep the bamboo stick horizontally diagonal as in the target, with the pepper visibly aligning at its point. No extra ingredients, no realistic rendering anywhere.

assets.correctionPrompt: Edit the RAISED ANATOMICAL LEFT HAND ONLY (the upper hand in the center-right of the character, holding the white VR controller with the blue ray aimed at the pepper). The error is CHIRALITY / PALM ORIENTATION, not arm pose. It currently looks like a second right hand with its BACK / knuckles facing the camera. Replace it with a correctly oriented LEFT HAND whose PALM / INNER WRIST is visibly facing the camera. Rotate the hand and wrist anatomy into a natural supinated grip, keeping a continuous forearm-to-palm connection. The viewer must clearly see the palm-side thumb base / thenar pad and the fleshy inner finger pads curling around the controller handle, NOT the broad back of the hand, outer knuckles, or fingernails. With the fingers angled up-right as in this pose, the LEFT thumb should be on the viewer-RIGHT side of that palm/grip (the opposite side from the erroneous right-hand-like grip), wrapping inward naturally onto the controller controls. The four fingers curl around the opposite side of the handle, with their inner pads partly visible to the camera. Render exactly one left thumb and four fingers, articulated in the same simple low-poly style. The grip should look like someone showing the inside of their LEFT hand while holding a VR controller, not like a mirrored right-hand dorsum. Adjust the controller's rotation slightly if needed so the actual HANDLE sits inside the palm; keep its white ring, blue ray and target position coherent. Do not mirror the entire image, limb, character or controller ray. Preserve both arm poses, elbows, sleeves and proportions exactly, except for the local raised left wrist rotation needed for the palmar view. Keep the lower/right hand completely unchanged. Keep the same person, face, hair, headset, apron, food skewer, ingredients, room, camera, lighting, colors and faceted matte LOW-POLY game-art style. No new text, borders, labels, watermarks, logos or extra fingers. This must be a visibly clear palm-side LEFT hand correction rather than another elbow or posture change.
